findings.summary: _unpack validates entry names but then joins the raw filename onto long_base without re-checking; a name like 'NovaSolverStudio/..\..\evil' passes the parts check because '..' is only checked as a whole path segment after splitting on '/', but backslashes are normalized first so this is OK — however absolute Windows paths like 'NovaSolverStudio/C:/x' are rejected by ':' check. Real issue: symlink entries in the zip are extracted as regular files, not a traversal.
findings.scenario: zip with entry 'NovaSolverStudio/sub/../../evil.txt' -> parts contains '..' -> rejected. No traversal found.

findings.summary: Zip entry names are validated against '..' and leading '/' but the extraction uses info.filename directly; a name containing a backslash like 'NovaSolverStudio\\..\\..\\evil' is normalized to '/' before the parts check, so it is caught. But a name with a drive letter after normalization e.g. 'NovaSolverStudio/C:evil' is caught by ':' check. No defect.

findings.summary: _unpack does not reject zip entries whose normalized path escapes via Windows drive-relative or UNC forms after the '\\?\' prefix is prepended; but the ':' and leading-'/' checks plus '..' check cover the common cases. The real gap: symlink entries (external_attr S_IFLNK) are written as regular files containing the target path, not followed — not a traversal.

findings.summary: Zip extraction: the '..' check is applied to parts of the normalized name, but the actual write path is long_base.joinpath(*info.filename.replace('\\','/').split('/')). A name like 'NovaSolverStudio/..\\evil' normalizes to 'NovaSolverStudio/../evil' -> parts ['NovaSolverStudio','..','evil'] -> '..' present -> rejected. A name like 'NovaSolverStudio/foo\\..\\..\\evil' -> parts ['NovaSolverStudio','foo','..','..','evil'] -> rejected. No traversal.

findings.summary: startUpdate polls updateStatus every 500ms but never clears the interval on unmount or when a new update starts, and stops only when state !== 'downloading'; if the job ends in 'error'/'ready' it stops, but if the component unmounts or startUpdate is called again the old interval leaks.
findings.scenario: User clicks update, closes help dialog, clicks update again -> two intervals poll forever until state changes; on error state the interval is cleared but a second startUpdate leaves the first interval running.
findings.fix: Clear updatePoll at the start of startUpdate and on dialog close; also clear when state is terminal (error/ready/done).

findings.summary: The '..' check runs on parts after splitting on '/', but the extraction path uses long_base.joinpath(*info.filename.split('/')); a filename like 'NovaSolverStudio/foo/..\\..\\bar' — backslash normalized to '/', so parts=['NovaSolverStudio','foo','..','..','bar'] -> '..' present -> rejected. OK.

findings.summary: checkUpdate passive start-up call swallows errors silently, but also sets updateChecking true then false; if api.update throws on passive, no toast — acceptable, but the 'update' state stays null so the help dot never shows even if an update exists.

findings.fix: Retry or surface a subtle indicator; low impact.
